key_insight: An adaptive black-box attack called immrag can extract many distinct images from multimodal retrieval systems by steering queries through embedding space using attacker-held and recovered images.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging tools that use image-returning retrieval, this highlights a privacy risk: confidential radiology images could be unintentionally exposed through the retrieval pipeline.
method: Blends a shadow image with a previously recovered image in each query.
Uses relevance-weighted resampling to explore embedding regions that still produce new retrievals.
Operates in a black-box setting against image-returning multimodal RAG systems.
evidence_signal: In experiments across medical assistant, document helper, and general-purpose settings, a single 2500-query run reconstructed up to 611 radiology images and outperformed a non-adaptive baseline by up to 5.6x in distinct items recovered.
watch_item: Results come from attack evaluations on specific retrievers and generators, so real-world risk may vary with system defenses, retrieval design, and access controls.
paper_title: Walking the Embedding Space: Datastore Extraction from Multimodal RAG
